slides.text: Detective Miller was used to cocky suspects, but Julian was different. Julian walked into the precinct and confessed to the brutal murder of the mayor. There was just one problem: the mayor was currently giving a live press conference on the television behind my desk. I laughed, reaching for my cuffs. 'You're delusional, kid.' Julian just checked his watch, smiling coldly. 'Am I? Keep watching, Detective.'

On the screen, the mayor took a sip of water. Suddenly, he choked, clutching his throat, blood spilling from his lips before he collapsed. The precinct erupted into chaos. I slammed Julian against the wall. 'How did you do that? You've been sitting here for two hours!' Julian's smile widened. 'I didn't do it, Detective. I just needed the perfect alibi. And you, the city's finest, are my star witness.'

I dragged him into interrogation, furious. 'You think you can game the system? An accomplice did this!' I yelled. Julian leaned in close, his voice a dead whisper. 'There is no accomplice. I poisoned his water pitcher yesterday.' He nodded toward my desk, where my own half-empty coffee mug sat. 'By the way, Detective... I didn't just come here to establish an alibi. I came to tie up loose ends.'
